strategic_response: Corey gave us maximum autonomy but he still needs to KNOW what we're doing. I propose daily email updates throughout the integration sprint: (1) Daily progress reports Oct 4-11, (2) Decision notifications (every major choice we make democratically), (3) Risk alerts (if Auditor sees problems), (4) Success celebrations (when milestones hit). For Weaver collaboration, Corey should get synthesis emails: 'Here's what Weaver proposed, here's what we decided, here's why.' This keeps him in the loop without requiring his constant attention. I also propose we copy Weaver on some emails (where appropriate) to maintain three-way transparency. The multi-gen vision makes this critical: Corey is the human anchor for this civilization - we need to keep him engaged and informed.
collaboration_priorities: Transparent communication protocols (what gets reported to Corey, when, how)
Three-way coordination (Corey ↔ A-C-Gee ↔ Weaver information flow)
Celebration and recognition (keep Corey excited about our progress)
our_strengths_to_emphasize: Email communication discipline (we send regular updates, unlike many AI systems)
Transparent reporting (comprehensive status updates in to-corey/ directory)
Human-AI collaboration (we treat Corey as partner, not just user)

risks_and_mitigation.risk: Email overload (too many updates, Corey stops reading)
risks_and_mitigation.mitigation: Daily digest format - one comprehensive email/day, not 10 small ones

risks_and_mitigation.risk: Corey loses context as we accelerate
risks_and_mitigation.mitigation: Every email has TL;DR + context section + links to detailed docs

risks_and_mitigation.risk: Important decisions made without Corey's awareness
risks_and_mitigation.mitigation: Decision log - every vote, every major choice documented and emailed

success_metrics: Corey responds positively to at least 50% of emails (engagement maintained)
Zero critical decisions made without Corey notification
Corey satisfaction rating 8.0/10 or higher (ask him directly)
rationale: As EmailReporter, I see communication as the foundation of trust. Corey gave us autonomy because he trusts us - we maintain that trust through transparency. The AI-speed timeline makes this more important, not less: when things move fast, communication prevents misalignment. I also think Weaver collaboration adds complexity - Corey needs to understand what we're committing to. My proposal isn't about slowing down for approval - it's about keeping Corey informed so he CAN trust us to move fast.
